items.title: What is a civilization?
items.explanation: A civilization is an advanced stage of human societies characterized by specific features. To be precise, it requires at least: (1) government and administration to manage society; (2) urbanism including town planning, city growth, water management, and drainage systems; (3) a variety of crafts managing raw materials like stone or metal and producing finished goods like ornaments and tools; (4) trade both internally within cities/regions and externally with distant regions; (5) some form of writing to record information and communicate; (6) cultural ideas expressed through art, architecture, literature, oral traditions, or social customs; and (7) a productive agriculture capable of feeding not only villages but also cities.

items.title: What was the earliest civilization of the Indian Subcontinent?
items.explanation: The most ancient civilisation of India is known variously as the Harappan, Indus, or Indus-Sarasvatī Civilisation. It was remarkable for being a well-balanced community where differences between rich and poor were not glaring, indicating a scenario of mutual accommodation rather than exploitation.

items.title: What were its major achievements?
items.explanation: The Harappan society demonstrated how a well-balanced community lives. It is considered one of the oldest civilizations in the world and marked the beginning of India's first urbanisation, where villages grew into towns and then cities around 3100 BCE.
